name: NERVE//CHOIR: Cooperative Neural Composition
description: NERVE//CHOIR is a cooperative BCI game for 4-to-12 players in which participants share partial neural state synchronization to co-compose and perform original music in real time, each player contributing emotional-somatic input that the game's engine translates into layered generative sound. The experience is described by players as 'being inside a piece of music that you are simultaneously dreaming and performing,' and session recordings have been released as standalone ambient albums that charted on mainstream feeds. The game occupies a strange space between instrument, game, and collective art practice.
story_hooks: A NERVE//CHOIR session group has been meeting weekly for two years and has begun experiencing memory bleed between sessions — waking with fragments of each other's dreams — and they're not sure they want it to stop.
Someone is using NERVE//CHOIR's partial neural sync architecture as a covert communication channel, embedding encoded information in the emotional-somatic input streams of unknowing players.
The 'Eighth Voice' recording has attracted the attention of a BCI research division that believes the unattributed sensory data came from a neural pattern that was officially declared dead in 2198.
